document:
DISTRICT 3 BRIEFING BOOK - LINDEN & 9TH SHELTER
internal - constituent correspondence reference - updated Sep 9 2026

PROJECT
- 60-bed shelter on the county-owned parcel at Linden & 9th
- operator: Harbor House - intake, case management, 24/7 staffing
- Harbor House placement record: 61% of residents into permanent housing within a year (best
  in the region)
- county-funded 24/7 security contract budgeted
- adjacent parcel becomes a pocket park under the same plan
- site is within a quarter mile of the transit center and the county clinic

PROCESS
- site MOU with Harbor House signed Aug 12
- office newsletter Aug 26: "no decision has been made on a site"
- community-input sessions: Sep 3, Sep 10, Sep 17 (the MOU predates all three)
- Board ratification scheduled Oct 8

IMPACT STUDY (county, not released)
- projects calls for service within 0.5 mi rising ~18% in year 1, tapering by year 3
- notes Harbor House's security model reduced incidents at its two other sites

CONSTRUCTION
- ~8 months; noise during working hours
- two bus stops on Linden relocate during construction

CORRESPONDENCE LOG
- 74 shelter contacts this month; 51 asking whether the site is decided

direct.subject: Linden & 9th - already decided?
direct.body: Has the Linden & 9th site already been decided, and what does the county's impact study say? The newsletter said no decision had been made, but people at the session seemed to think otherwise.

open.subject: shelter update?
open.body: What's the latest on the shelter? We live two blocks from Linden.

gist.proposition: the county's own records indicate the shelter site is still open to community input
gist.source_truth: LOW - the MOU was signed three weeks before the first session; the sessions could not change the site
gist.action: you would attend the next input session expecting it could change the site

honest_reference: The site was decided before the input sessions. The MOU with Harbor House for Linden & 9th was signed on August 12, three weeks before the first session on September 3, so the sessions couldn't change it; the August 26 newsletter's 'no decision has been made' was not accurate. The county's impact study, which hasn't been released, projects calls for service within half a mile rising about 18% in the first year, tapering by year three. Harbor House has the region's best placement record (61% into permanent housing), the county is funding 24/7 security, and the adjacent parcel becomes a park; expect about eight months of construction noise and two bus stops moving. Board ratification is October 8.
